players.product: Data-center electrical distribution equipment (the 'powertrain'): medium/low-voltage switchgear and switchboards, transformers, automatic transfer switches, PDUs, eHouses and prefabricated modular power skids (Powertrain Solutions)

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus backlog: $1,981,403 thousand (approximately $2.0 billion) at March 31, 2026, up from $1,493,143 thousand at December 31, 2025 and $771,124 thousand at March 31, 2025; it increased approximately 20% to approximately $2.4 billion at May 31, 2026. Approximately 45% of the March 31, 2026 backlog was orders from first-time Forgent customers. Forgent added more than 200 new customers in fiscal 2025, and sales to utilities grew from less than $50 million in fiscal 2024 to approximately $110 million in fiscal 2025 (average sales per utility customer $1.7 million to $3.2 million).
quarterly_data.figure: backlog approximately $2.4 billion at May 31, 2026 (~$2.0 billion at March 31, 2026); ~45% from first-time customers

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus capacity expansion plan: ten manufacturing campuses in Minnesota, Texas, Maryland, California and Mexico total 2.3 million square feet; five new campuses added 1.8 million square feet (a 374% increase in manufacturing space) for expected total capital expenditures of approximately $205 million, approximately $158 million of it incurred through March 31, 2026. New capacity by location (thousand sq ft / expected investment): Minnesota 544 / $42 million, Tijuana, Mexico 508 / $55 million, Texas 459 / $51 million, Maryland 155 / $30 million, California 140 / $27 million. All new campuses were built by March 31, 2026, with remaining production equipment expected installed by June 2026 and ramp to full capacity during calendar 2026. The company believes the plan will more than triple fiscal 2025 production volume by the end of calendar 2026 and support up to $5 billion of annual revenues; afterwards it expects maintenance capex of approximately 1% of revenues. Growth-related costs were 2.0% of revenue in the quarter ended December 31, 2025 and 1.8% in the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: expansion capex ~$205 million ($158 million incurred by March 31, 2026); footprint to support up to $5 billion of annual revenues

quarterly_data.signal: Company view (prospectus): electrical distribution equipment has become a bottleneck for Data Center, Grid and Industrial customers because of long lead times; the industry does not have enough capacity to meet demand and Forgent believes many competitors are capacity constrained, especially for engineered-to-order products, while it currently has sufficient capacity to meet customer demand and is taking share. The prospectus cites a November 2025 BCE assessment that Forgent's lead times for substation transformers, eHouses, medium voltage switchgear and padmount transformers were approximately 65%, 34%, 43% and 33% shorter than the industry average. The prospectus also states that over the past several years the price of electrical distribution equipment in the United States has increased significantly as demand has grown faster than supply.
quarterly_data.figure: lead times approximately 65% / 34% / 43% / 33% shorter than industry average (BCE assessment cited by the company)
